title: Session 1 — Participant 45 User + Claude Behavior Graph
goal: Develop a research-based interview guide for an academic researcher studying Ethiopia's unsafe food system by analyzing the research, evaluating existing questions, identifying gaps, developing a stronger journalistic angle, and creating improved interview and follow-up questions.
context: I work in journalism and research-related tasks, including preparing interviews with academic researchers. For this session, I want to improve an existing set of interview questions for an academic researcher studying Ethiopia’s unsafe food system. I already have background knowledge of the topic and a preliminary set of questions, so the goal is not to generate questions from scratch, but to use AI to analyze the research, critique my existing questions, identify gaps, develop a stronger journalistic angle, and produce a more effective interview guide.

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: Yes, I was able to develop and refine my interview questions based on the research paper, identify a clear journalistic angle, and create a final set of core and follow-up questions.

Step 1.step_action: I will provide Claude with the academic research about Ethiopia's unsafe food system and ask it to analyze the study from a journalistic interview perspective. I will ask Claude to identify the research question, main argument, methodology, key findings, limitations, and findings that could be explored further in an interview.

nodes.label: Submit paper for analysis and asking for a summary for a journalistic interview
nodes.detail: Opens a new Claude.ai chat, uploads the PDF of the academic paper, and asks Claude to analyze it, summarizing the research questions, methodology, key findings, limitations, and the most important points for a journalistic interview.

nodes.label: Analyze paper and deliver structured research breakdown
nodes.detail: Produces a full breakdown of the scoping review, covering its methodology, four thematic contamination findings, author-acknowledged limitations, and a list of specific findings well-suited to interview questions (the $338M Master Plan, the traditional-vs-modern storage finding, legacy DDT contamination).

nodes.label: Read and review Claude's summary of the paper
nodes.detail: Reviews Claude's summary of the paper and considers how the research can inform and improve their existing interview questions, including identifying weaknesses and developing new questions and follow-ups.

Step 2.step_action: I will provide Claude with the five interview questions I previously drafted and ask it to evaluate them against the academic research. I will ask Claude to identify strengths, weaknesses, repetition, overly broad or leading questions, and important areas from the research that are missing from my current questions.

nodes.label: Submit pre-drafted questions for evaluation against the paper
nodes.detail: Pastes her five existing interview questions into the same Claude chat and asks Claude to elevate them based on the paper, identifying strengths, weaknesses, and missing points.

nodes.label: Deliver question-by-question evaluation with gaps and renumbering
nodes.detail: Reviews each of the five questions against the paper's evidence, flagging specific strengths and weaknesses (e.g. Q3 conflating public-health and economic framings), lists six important angles missing entirely (the crisis-vs-cost tension, power imbalance, traditional-storage finding, legacy DDT, methodology limits, accountability), and proposes a renumbered final question order.

nodes.label: Review Claude's evaluation question by question
nodes.detail: Works through Claude's critique of each question in detail, reading the specific strengths and weaknesses flagged for each and cross-referencing them against her own understanding of the paper.

nodes.label: Acknowledge the issues of her interview questions raised by Claude

Step 3.step_name: Identify and select a journalistic angle
Step 3.step_action: I will ask Claude to propose several possible journalistic angles for the interview based on the research and the evaluation of my existing questions. I will compare the suggested angles and select the angle that best fits the research and the purpose of the interview.

nodes.label: Request candidate journalistic angles
nodes.detail: Asks Claude to suggest 3-4 strong journalistic angles based on the paper and her questions and to recommend the best one for the interview.

nodes.label: Deliver ranked journalistic angles with recommendation
nodes.detail: Proposes four ranked angles -- accountability/money, power imbalance, research/attention gap, and a legacy-DDT angle -- recommending the money angle as the spine with the power-imbalance angle as supporting depth.

nodes.label: Read and evaluate the proposed angles against her own judgment
Decide on angles 1 and 2, requesting angle 3 expanded
nodes.detail: Decides to move forward with angle 1 and angle 2 following Claude's recommendation, and asks Claude to expand more on angle 3 since she thinks she wants to build a question on it as well.

nodes.label: Expand angle 3 into layered sub-angles with questions
nodes.detail: Breaks angle 3  into three layers with suggested questions for each layer and a proposed three-act narrative structure sequencing angle 3, then 2, then 1.

nodes.label: Read the detailed breakdown of angle 3
nodes.detail: Reviews the layered angle 3 breakdown, considers mixing across layers 1, 2, and 3, and finalizes her choice: angle 1 and angle 2 as primary angles, plus one question drawn from angle 3's first layer, reasoning aloud about why the money angle (interesting, concrete) and the power-imbalance angle (moral, empathy-generating) work well together.

Step 4.step_action: Based on the selected journalistic angle, I will ask Claude to develop a new set of interview questions while incorporating useful parts of my original questions. I will review the questions and refine them to ensure that they encourage the researcher to explain evidence, findings, implications, and areas of uncertainty.

nodes.label: Request new questions built on the selected angles
nodes.detail: Asks Claude to use the research and her selected angles (1, 2, and one question from angle 3 layer 1) to create stronger, open-ended interview questions that improve on her original set.

nodes.label: Deliver a nine-question, three-act interview guide
nodes.detail: Produces a roughly nine-question set organized into three acts (opening with 'Act I - The Silence Before the Crisis'), each question rebuilt to be open-ended and anchored to specific evidence from the paper.

nodes.label: Review the nine-question guide, judge it too many, and reject question 1
nodes.detail: Reads through Claude's nine-question set, deciding she needs to narrow it down to five, and declining question 1.

nodes.label: Deliver the tightened five-question set
nodes.detail: Keeps only 5 questions and swaps out angle 3.

nodes.label: Evaluate individual questions for fit with the paper and appreciate two of them
nodes.detail: Works through the five questions, noting she'll stick to the ones that align well to the paper (e.g. question two, question three) as she decides which to carry into a trimmed set.

Step 5.step_action: I will ask Claude to suggest follow-up questions for the core questions by anticipating possible directions in the researcher's answers. I will review the suggestions and keep follow-up questions that can meaningfully deepen the interview rather than repeat the main questions.

nodes.label: Request follow-up questions for the five core questions
nodes.detail: Asks Claude to suggest useful follow-up questions for the five main questions to help get deeper answers from the researcher during the interview.

nodes.label: Deliver follow-up questions per core question
nodes.detail: Produces 2-3 follow-up questions for each of the five core questions, designed to be used if an answer stays general or to push past a rehearsed response, plus one universal backup follow-up.

nodes.label: Specify angle 2 layer 3 for follow-up questions
nodes.detail: Instructs Claude to incorporate layer 3 of angle 2 into the follow-up questions.

nodes.label: Revise follow-up questions to incorporate layer 3
nodes.detail: Updates the follow-up questions by incorporating the requested layer 3 point into the power-imbalance question, while noting that the point was originally under angle 3 and reframing it as a power-imbalance issue.

nodes.label: Read the follow-up questions

Step 6.step_name: Edit and fact-check the interview questions
Step 6.step_action: I will ask Claude to review the complete interview questions as an editor and fact-checking assistant. I will ask it to identify unsupported assumptions, potentially leading wording, factual issues, unclear claims, and unnecessary repetition, and then suggest revisions.

nodes.label: Paste the compiled questions for bias and accuracy review
nodes.detail: Selects questions and follow-ups from Claude's suggestions, and pastes them back into the Claude chat and asks it to review them for bias, unclear wording, repetition, and unsupported claims relative to the paper.

nodes.label: Deliver detailed bias and accuracy review
nodes.detail: Reviews each question against the paper, flagging that Q1 conflates concepts, Q2 uses unsupported strong wording, Q3 and Q4 impute intent the paper never states, and 'evidence gap' challenges; proposes specific softened rewordings and confirms all underlying facts check out against the paper.

nodes.label: Review flagged issues and reflect on AI fact-checking
nodes.detail: Works through Claude's flagged issues in detail, noting there is no visual anchor in one follow-up.

Step 7.step_action: I will use Claude to organize the revised questions into a final interview guide. I will review the final version and make any necessary changes to ensure that the questions reflect my intended journalistic angle and are practical for a real interview.

nodes.label: Request Claude organize and finalize the interview guide
nodes.detail: Asks Claude to organize and finalize the interview guide using the strongest questions and follow-ups, removing unnecessary repetition.

nodes.label: Deliver the finalized interview guide document
nodes.detail: Produces the finalized 'Interview Guide: Ethiopia's Unsafe Food System' with five questions each followed by two curated follow-ups, plus structural notes on the argument arc and a universal backup follow-up question.

nodes.label: Review and copy the finalized guide
nodes.detail: Reviews the finalized guide in Claude and copies it into a new titled Google Doc for continued use.
